pass_a_gloss: And if the one saying: you will not make for yourself an idol nor a likeness of anything and the next things, says these things, the 'you will not bow down to them' and the 'nor may you serve them', as these differing toward each other, perhaps the one disposed toward the idols serves them, but the one not disposed, but through cowardice, which he names going-along-with, playing the hypocrite toward them for the sake of seeming like the many to be pious, does not serve but bows down to the idols. And I would say that those at the court swearing off the Christianity, or before the court, do not serve but bow down to the idols, taking the name of the Lord God, the 'God', upon vain and soulless matter. And so the people profaned into the daughters of Moab were bowing down and were not serving idols. It has been written at least in the very words that they called them upon the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate of their sacrifices, and they bowed down to their idols and were consecrated to Beelphegor. And observe that it has not been said: and they served their idols; for neither was it possible, after so many signs and wonders, under one tilt of the moment, to be persuaded by the women with whom they were whoring to deem the idols gods. And perhaps so also at the calf-making in Exodus they bowed down, not serving the calf which they watched coming to be. A trial then and testing-place of the love toward the divine we must deem to have happened the standing temptation. For the Lord will test you, as has been written in Deuteronomy, to know if you love the Lord your God out of your whole heart and out of your whole soul. But you, being tested, will go behind the Lord your God and will fear him and will guard his commands, and most of all the: there will not be to you other gods except me, and will hear his voice and be added to him, he taking you from the regions here and adding you to himself into the, as the apostle named it, increase of God in him.
pass_b_english: If the one who says, “You shall not make for yourself an idol, nor a likeness of anything” (Exodus 20:4), and what follows, says both “You shall not bow down to them” and “Nor shall you serve them” (Exodus 20:5), as though these differ from each other, then perhaps the one who is devoted to idols serves them, while the one who is not devoted to them, but out of cowardice, which he calls accommodation, makes a pretence towards them so as to seem as pious as the many, does not serve the idols but does bow down to them. And I would say that those who forswear Christianity at the tribunal, or before the tribunal, do not serve the idols but do bow down to them, applying the name of the Lord God, the name “God”, to vain and lifeless matter.

In this way too the people who were defiled “with the daughters of Moab” (Numbers 25:1) bowed down to idols and did not serve them. It is written, in so many words: “They called them to the sacrifices of their idols, and the people ate of their sacrifices, and bowed down to their idols, and were initiated into the rites of Baal-Peor” (Numbers 25:2-3). And notice that it is not said, “and they served their idols”. For it was not possible, after so many signs and wonders, for them to be persuaded in a single turn of the moment, by the women with whom they were committing fornication, to think the idols were gods. Perhaps it was in this way too, at the making of the calf in Exodus, that they “bowed down” (Exodus 32:8), without serving the calf, which they had watched being made.

So we must think that the present temptation has come about as a test and a proving of our love for God. “For the Lord will test you”, as it is written in Deuteronomy, “to know whether you love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul” (Deuteronomy 13:3). But you, when you are tested, “will walk after the Lord your God and fear him and keep his commandments”, above all the one, “You shall have no other gods besides me” (Exodus 20:3), “and you will hear his voice and be joined to him” (Deuteronomy 13:4), who takes you from the places here and joins you to himself, into what the apostle called “the growth of God” in him (Colossians 2:19).

choices.choice: 2026-11-11: retranslated in full from Koetschau (GCS 2, ch. VI); the old English was a digest; the old entry under this id was attached to the wrong chapter and lost the distinction between bowing down and serving, the Baal-Peor and calf examples and the Deuteronomy 13 testing.
Checked against the Patristic Text Archive digitisation of Koetschau (pta0007.pta007.pta-grc1), which reads ὡς διαφερόντων, “as though these differ”.

Read λατρεύει (OCR λατρεύεε), δικαστηρίου, ὄνομα (OCR οὔνομα), εἰς τὰς θυγατέρας, τοσαῦτα (OCR τοῦσαὔτα), προσεκύνησαν, αὐτόν (OCR αἰτόν), τὴν, καὶ τῆς φωνῆς αὐτοῦ ἀκούσεσθε (PTA), λαμβάνοντι μὲν (OCR δὲν; PTA μὲν), αὔξησιν.
“were initiated into the rites of Baal-Peor”, following the Septuagint verb (be initiated), not the English Bible's “joined himself”.
“accommodation”: going along with others; Origen reports it as the coward's own name for his cowardice.
